skill.name: xcrawl-search
skill.description: Use this skill for XCrawl search tasks, including keyword search request design, location and language controls, result analysis, and follow-up crawl or scrape planning.
skill.summary: Run XCrawl keyword searches with location, language, and result limits, then return the upstream response.
skill.author: xcrawl-api

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match Markdown formatting, placeholders, or documented XCrawl authentication and search operations rather than dangerous execution. The cURL example exposes the bearer token in process arguments, creating a local credential disclosure risk. No evidence found of prompt injection, unrelated credential collection, or unauthorized data transfers.

remediation.issue: The cURL Authorization argument includes the expanded API key, which can appear in process listings or command telemetry.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer the Node fetch example, which constructs authentication in memory, or supply cURL headers through standard input without exposing secrets in arguments.

remediation.issue: The local credential configuration guidance does not specify restrictive file permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Document owner-only directory and file permissions, and prohibit logging the configuration or including it in version control.

content.value_statement: Web research needs explicit queries and consistent search settings. This skill guides XCrawl search requests with location, language, and result limits, then returns upstream responses.
actual_capabilities: Build keyword search requests for the XCrawl search endpoint.
Set location, language, and result limits from 1 to 100.
Read the XCrawl API key from a local JSON configuration file.
Execute documented requests through cURL or Node.
Return the endpoint, request payload, raw response body, and failure details.
Produce relevance summaries when the user explicitly requests them.
limitations: Requires an XCrawl account, available credits, a configured API key, and network access.
Default output is the raw response, not a synthesized research report.
Location targeting is best effort, and ranking guarantees are not documented.
Detailed result fields are implementation-defined; crawling and scraping execution are outside the documented search workflow.

use_cases.title: Find Research Sources
use_cases.description: Search a defined topic with explicit geography and language, then inspect the upstream results for candidate sources.

use_cases.title: Inspect API Responses
use_cases.description: Run a bounded search request and examine response metadata, credit usage, and failures before building an integration.

use_cases.title: Explore Regional Topics
use_cases.description: Search the same topic with different location and language settings to gather region-specific source candidates.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Search XCrawl for [topic] with a limit of 10 results. Return the endpoint, request settings, and raw response.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: perform one bounded keyword search.

prompt_templates.title: Localize a Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Search XCrawl for [topic] in [location], using language [ISO language code] and a limit of 20. Return the raw response.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: specify regional and language settings.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Search Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Search XCrawl for [topic] with a limit of 15. Summarize relevance using only returned evidence, and separate your summary from the raw response.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Regional Searches
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan two XCrawl searches for [topic] using [location A] and [location B]. Use 10 results each and request approval before execution. Report returned credit usage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare explicit requests with a review step.

output_examples.input: Show the settings for a US English search about AI web crawler APIs with 20 results.
output: Illustrative request preview; no live search was performed.
Query: AI web crawler API. Location: US. Language: en. Result limit: 20.
The executed request would return the upstream response body without a default summary.

output_examples.input: Explain the response fields available after a search.
output: The documented response includes a search task identifier, endpoint, version, status, and query.
It also includes result data, start and end timestamps, and total credits used.
Detailed result fields depend on the provider implementation.
No live results or credit totals are implied by this example.

best_practices: Use explicit queries, supported language codes, and small result limits before expanding a search.
Protect the local credential file and prefer Node authentication to avoid placing tokens in process arguments.
Inspect returned errors and credit usage, and request summaries explicitly when needed.
anti_patterns: Include private credentials or confidential internal information in search queries.
Assume undocumented filters, ranking guarantees, or a fixed detailed result schema.
Request large repeated searches without reviewing credit consumption.

faq.question: What does this skill search?
faq.answer: It sends keyword queries to the XCrawl Search API and returns the upstream response.

faq.question: Where is the API key stored?
faq.answer: The documented setup reads XCRAWL_API_KEY from ~/.xcrawl/config.json. Global environment variables are not required.

faq.question: Which search settings are documented?
faq.answer: The request supports query, location, language, and limit. Defaults are US, en, and 10 results; the limit range is 1 to 100.

faq.question: Does the skill summarize results automatically?
faq.answer: No. It returns raw responses by default and creates summaries only when explicitly requested.

faq.question: Does using XCrawl consume credits?
faq.answer: Yes. Requests consume provider credits. Check current account terms and inspect returned credit usage.

faq.question: Does this skill crawl or scrape discovered pages?
faq.answer: The documented execution workflow covers search only. It does not provide crawl or scrape execution examples.
